question.text: A company announces a buyback through tender offer. Sunita holds shares worth Rs.1.8 lakh (market value on record date). Which category does she fall under?

answer.text: Small shareholder category, as her holding value does not exceed Rs.2 lakh on the record date

explanation.text: The Logic: A small shareholder in a tender-offer buyback is one whose market value of shares on the record date is not more than Rs.2 lakh. Sunita's Rs.1.8 lakh holding fits within this limit, so she falls under the small shareholder category. The Trap: Candidates may use purchase price or face value instead of the market value on the record date. The classification is strictly based on market value as on the record date. Note: 15% of the buyback is reserved for the small shareholder category under the source.
